newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian inflation rises slightly in July.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian inflation rises slightly in July.

text.p: Nigeria's consumer price inflation rose to 29.5 percent in July this year from 28.8 percent in June, government figures released on Thursday showed.
"Some of the items that were responsible for the rise include food, clothing materials, rent and textbooks," the federal office of statistics said.
Inflation, however, remained inside the target zone of 20-30 percent set by the military government in its 1996 budget.
It fell below 30 percent barrier in June this year for the first time since February 1992.

The government says war on inflation is the goal of a tight fiscal policy that has persisted from 1995 through the 1996 budget. The policy has stabilised various sectors of the economy, but has yet to induce real growth.
Independent experts, who have hailed the downward trend in inflation, said steps must be taken to continue to keep prices down.
"The major challenge of the 1997 budget is the stimulation of growth while keeping inflation under check," the umbrella association of chambers of commerce and industry said.
